No test is skipped with a reason that contradicts the environment, such as 'not installed' while the package is installed. Live-endpoint tests appear only under their marker.

The refusal is a dedicated named input refusal returned with status 422 and a refusal_type, and it is raised before any vector store is constructed. No directory is create...

This covers ForbiddenSelectorInputError (a hash-shaped alias or harness in the selector of /query, /compare, POST /documents and the DELETE /documents body), AmbiguousIngestPayloadEr...

The MCP transport returns a JSON refusal for every refusal REST returns: the ToolError text parses as JSON and carries refusal_type. This covers AmbiguousIngestPayloadError and OversizedDocumentError from ingest (today they are wrapped in pydantic.ValidationError and surface as UnexpectedToolError with no reason), Page bound errors from status, and the scope-precondition errors: scope job witho...

Not-found lookups return HTTP 404 with the refusal body: UnknownTraceReferenceError (/trace/resolve), UnknownJobError (GET /jobs/{id}), UnresolvableEvidenceReferenceError (/evidence/resolve) and UnknownGenerationVersionError. All other refusals stay 422. The status code for each refusal type comes from one mapping in rest.py, and the rest.py comment describes that mapping.

ForeignEngineRefusalError is reported as a server-side failure, not as a 422 caller refusal (proposed: 502). Its public body does not contain raw subprocess stderr: 'message' names only the operation and the exception class, 'cause' is not copied into 'message', and the stderr/traceback text (absolute server paths, env-var names) is not in the default response. That text is logged server-side a...

GET /corpus, GET /corpus/counts and GET /jobs/{id} never return an unstructured 500 when the v1 corpus adapter fails. MissingV1InterpreterError, CorpusOpSubprocessError, CorpusOpTimeoutError and a JSON decode error each return the structured machine-fault response chosen in SEAM-05 (a refusal_type naming the failure, no stderr). The OpenAPI schema for these three routes declares that response.

No ingest input from the caller produces HTTP 500 or an MCP UnexpectedToolError. (a) POST /documents/upload with a file over 26,214,400 bytes returns 422 OversizedDocumentError. (b) The shared document_id check (generated_on_disk_name) uses fullmatch against ^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$. A caller document_id that fails it (for example '../x', 'a.b', 'a\n') on POST /documents, POST /documents/upload, MCP in...

Page size and offset are bounded on every path. A limit outside 1..100 or an offset below 0 is refused with a named refusal and never clamped, on GET /corpus, GET /jobs/{id}, MCP status and in-process Page construction. As a result, limit=0 and negative limits never reach the v1 driver slice, no response contains more than 100 documents, and next_offset always advances or is null. The Page docs...

Empty inputs are refused instead of being run or enqueued. Query text that is '' or whitespace-only returns EmptyQueryObjectError before any node runs: no LLM or embedding call, and no trace is persisted. Text ingest with '' or whitespace-only text, a 0-byte upload, and MCP raw_base64 '' are refused (AmbiguousIngestPayloadError or a dedicated empty-document refusal), and nothing is written to c...

Selector(capability=[]) is refused with a named refusal on every route that accepts a selector (/query, /compare, /documents, /documents/upload, DELETE /documents, and the MCP tools). It never resolves to the bypass wiring, never renders an empty compare key, and no node runs.

POST /compare detects every comparison-key collision before any arm executes, and each arm executes exactly the wiring that the pre-check resolved. The selector pairs [{},{}], [{alias:'default'},{}], [{alias:'x'},{harness:'x'}] and [{alias:'a+b'},{capability:['a','b']}] each either produce distinct keys or return 422 DuplicateComparisonKeyError with zero arms run, zero LLM/embedding calls and z...

POST /promote refuses, with a named refusal, an alias that is empty or that no Selector could carry (one that matches the hash shape ^(sha256:)?[0-9a-f]{64}$), and writes no ledger row. Every alias that can be promoted is therefore selectable afterwards.

On POST /documents/upload, a selector form field that holds the JSON literal 'null' or an empty string means 'no selector' (the default wiring). This is the same as omitting the field and the same as selector null on the JSON routes.

Every concrete SeamRefusalError subclass that a transport can return is exported from one refusal catalogue (refusals.__all__ or a documented re-export list). This includes NoRawUploadPathForModalityError, UnknownTraceReferenceError, UnresolvableEvidenceReferenceError, UnbudgetableParticipantError and every refusal added in this phase, so a typed client generated from the catalogue covers every...

Seam docstrings and dead code match the behaviour. The rest.py promote docstrings say that a non-string verb is a validation error and that only a non-member string gives UnrecognisedPromotionVerbError. The rest.py module docstring says one handler is registered on SeamRefusalError and matches subclasses through the MRO. selectors._DEFAULT_ARM and selectors._ARM_NAMES are removed (tests import ...

One of t...

When constructing any store in _build_stores fails (for example the graph open raising under the lock in STOR-01), every store already opened in that call (kv, vector) is finalized before the exception leaves the engine method. Store construction happens inside the try/finally in ingest, delete_document, _execute and resolve_evidence. Repeated failed requests open zero additional sqlite connect...

POST /evidence/resolve opens only the vector namespace named in the EvidenceRef. It constructs no SqliteKVStore or CozoGraphStore and creates no text_chunks or chunk_entity_relation directory. It succeeds while the graph namespace is held by another call. N successive resolve calls against an unchanged index read and SHA-256-hash the index file once, not N times. After the index files change (f...

GET /health is read-only and reports store state accurately. On an empty store_root it creates no directories or files (no text_chunks/kv.sqlite3, no chunk_entity_relation/graph.cozo, no Cozo relations) and reports missing stores as absent, not ok. The vector entry opens the modality's vector namespaces and reports false when a Faiss index is corrupted (VectorStoreCorruptedError), instead of al...

Capability scoping is enforced per access mode. A node that declares only reads_kv, reads_vector or reads_graph receives a handle on which every mutating method raises UndeclaredEffectError: upsert, delete, delete_by_ids, upsert_node, upsert_edge, delete_node, delete_edge, drop and index_done_callback, including on a FaissVectorStore returned by select() from a read-only MultiNamespaceVectorSto...

An ingest whose wiring records any node failure commits nothing. When run_wiring returns node_exceptions, the engine calls drop_pending_index_ops on every store instead of index_done_callback, then raises ForeignEngineRefusalError. After a refused HippoRAG ingest, the kv and vector stores hold no records for that document_id, and query evidence cannot return its chunks.

delete_document builds its stores with the resolved wiring's store_namespaces. It flushes every store (index_done_callback) when the delete run succeeds and drops pending ops when it fails. FaissVectorStore.delete_by_ids buffers deletions until index_done_callback, as kv, graph and lexical do, so drop_pending_index_ops reverts a vector delete. After a successful delete, the kv, graph and vector...

Opening a FaissVectorStore whose directory holds vector.faiss without vector.meta.json, or vector.meta.json without vector.faiss, raises VectorStoreCorruptedError, as the module docstring states. It does not open an empty store that the next flush overwrites. Evidence resolve against such a namespace returns the corruption refusal, not 'record no longer present'.

FaissVectorStore and MultiNamespaceVectorStore report named refusals for invalid input. query with top_k <= 0 raises a named ValueError subclass instead of a bare AssertionError. The 'available vector namespaces' list in VectorNamespaceNotSelectedError contains only directories that hold vector.faiss. Calling score_all, self_knn, get_by_id or iter_vectors on an unselected MultiNamespaceVectorSt...

CozoGraphStore keeps edges consistent with nodes. After a flushed delete_node('x'), get_node_edges('x') returns [], node_degree of every former neighbour excludes edges to x, and export_to_igraph contains no dangling edge. upsert_edge with an endpoint that does not exist (committed or pending) is refused or creates the node, depending on the owner decision, and never leaves a dangling edge.

SqliteKVStore keeps its pending buffer separate from callers. get_by_id returns a copy, so mutating it does not change the buffered record, and upsert stores a copy of the caller's dict. is_empty returns True when every committed and pending row is pending deletion.

Every store effect the effect vocabulary accepts (reads_lexical, writes_lexical, reads_blob, writes_artifact) meets one of two conditions. Either it resolves to a store wired by _build_stores at run time, or a wiring with a node that both declares it and needs its store is refused at parse_wiring with a named refusal. No wiring parses successfully and then fails at run time with StoreNotWiredEr...

FilesystemBlobStore validates digests against ^[0-9a-f]{64}$ inside the store. get, read_range and delete refuse '../../etc/hostname' and any digest containing '/' or '..' with a named refusal, and never touch a path outside the blob root. put removes its temp file when write_bytes or os.replace raises. read_range refuses a negative length.

SqliteLexicalStore.query('alpha beta') matches documents that contain both terms in any position, with each term bound and quoted separately and combined with AND, as the module docstring states. Returned scores follow the vector store convention: higher is better, sorted descending.

Quarantined-namespace GC is a real operation. gc_namespace has a production caller that removes an instance's quarantined namespace directories when that instance is retired or torn down. A removal failure other than 'directory absent' raises a named refusal instead of being suppressed by ignore_errors=True. The namespaces.py D-07 docstring matches the actual layout: either the seam stores deri...
FaissVectorStore.upsert refuses metadata containing the keys 'id' or 'score' with a named refusal. Results from get_by_id, query, score_all and self_knn always carry the real id and score.

Every LightRAG corpus operation (ingest, delete, and the status ops behind GET /corpus, /corpus/counts, /jobs/{job_id} and the /health engine probe) passes run_corpus_op a v1 working_dir derived from the app's store_root and workspace, never the repo-global DEFAULT_V1_WORKING_DIR (v1/.corpus_working_dir). Two apps built with different store_root values do not see each other's documents on GET /...

A document ingested through POST /documents with the default (LightRAG) selector becomes retrievable by POST /query on the LightRAG arms and resolvable by POST /evidence/resolve, and after DELETE /documents/{id} returns success its chunks are no longer returned by /query or resolvable by /evidence/resolve. full-delete only reports graph/vector/kv store touches for stores it actually changed.

The lightrag full-ingest part declares mutates_store (not writes_artifact with scope quarantined), its admission record names the storage it actually writes, and engine.ingest runs the wiring with a seam-event recorder so a successful LightRAG ingest emits MACH-11 seam events for the stores it touched, as full-delete does.

Concurrent LightRAG writes to one working dir are serialized: while a LightRAG ingest or delete subprocess is running against a working dir, a second ingest or delete for the same working dir either waits for it to finish or is refused with a named error (not run in parallel), so no run's doc-status/KV/graph writes overwrite another's.

Adapter input and failures are validated, named and readable: CorpusOpSubprocessError keeps the last 2000 characters of v1 stderr (so the traceback's exception line is included); non-JSON driver stdout raises a named refusal instead of JSONDecodeError; failures on the status/job/counts routes map to a named 4xx/5xx refusal body instead of an unstructured 500; ForeignEngineRefusalError.cause ret...

When the v1 configuration keys required by the driver (EMBEDDING_DIM, EMBEDDING_MODEL, EMBEDDING_BINDING_HOST, EMBEDDING_BINDING_API_KEY, LIGHTRAG_KV_STORAGE/GRAPH_STORAGE/VECTOR_STORAGE/DOC_STATUS_STORAGE) are missing from the process environment, v1/.env.parity and v1/.env, ingest/delete/status/counts/jobs return a named 'v1 not configured' refusal listing the missing key names (never values)...

A LightRAG ingest that exceeds its wall-clock ceiling (900 s ingest, 300 s delete, 60 s status) marks its document as stuck/interrupted: GET /corpus reports any document left in PARSING/ANALYZING/PROCESSING with no job in flight under a distinguishable stuck/interrupted status, an explicit retry/reprocess action exists for it, and the next unrelated ingest does not reprocess it inside its own r...

POST /documents/upload (and POST /documents with raw) on the LightRAG path indexes the uploaded file's content: the stored chunks contain text from the uploaded bytes, the file extension is taken from a validated suffix of file_name, and a second upload with different content under a new document_id is processed normally instead of being rejected as a content-hash duplicate (dup-<md5> FAILED ro...

Raw upload inbox files are scoped per workspace (<store_root>/<workspace>/corpus-inbox or equivalent) and removed once v1 has read them or the ingest has been refused, and DELETE /documents/{id} removes any remaining inbox file for that id; no corpus-inbox file outlives its job.

IngestJob.enqueued reports the number of documents v1 actually enqueued: when v1 drops the document (existing document_id, same basename, same content hash) the response reports enqueued 0 (or a named duplicate refusal) instead of 200 enqueued 1, and IngestJob.job_id is the track_id v1 recorded for the run.

LightRAG write-side LLM spend is metered: corpus-delete.json and the full-delete part declare calls_llm, the v1 driver returns token usage for ingest and delete when v1 records it, and full-ingest/full-delete report counted_by other than 'unbudgetable' when usage is present (the usage-present branch in full_ingest.py:226-233 is reachable or removed).

The full-ingest and full-delete admission records number CONTRACT §8 conditions correctly: network-namespace isolation and token unbudgetability are recorded under condition 3, condition 8 records the ~90-day TTL with ledger renewal, and condition 9 records part_ref invocation counting, matching codebase_memory_mcp.py:241-263; the full_ingest.py module docstring states the same mapping.

GET /health performs no writes: on a fresh, empty store_root it creates no files or directories (no <workspace>/text_chunks/kv.sqlite3, no <workspace>/chunk_entity_relation/graph.cozo, no v1/.corpus_working_dir or per-workspace v1 working dir).

GET /health reports only facts it checked: stores.vector reflects an actual Faiss index probe or is reported as not probed; an empty or unused store_root is not reported 'ok'; the namespaces probed include the HippoRAG ones (hipporag-text-chunks, hipporag-graph) as well as LightRAG's; status is not 'ok' when the app has no LLM/embedding clients; working_dir_present reports the directory's exist...

eval corpus_ingest --spend --arm lightrag writes only to the eval store (v1/.eval_corpus_store or the configured eval working dir), never to the operator corpus v1/.corpus_working_dir, so GET /corpus does not list eval documents; and aa_run run after that ingest retrieves evidence from the ingested eval documents with the LightRAG arm it names, instead of scoring zero over empty v2 namespaces.

Querying a LightRAG arm whose vector namespace (chunks, entities, relationships) has never been populated returns a named refusal or an explicit 'namespace empty' signal in the envelope, distinguishable from a populated namespace with no matches; MultiNamespaceVectorStore.select() on an unknown namespace in a read path does not silently create an empty store.

LightRAG hybrid/local/global answers are generated from KG context as in v1 kg_query: the assembled prompt includes the budgeted entity and relation descriptions (budget-entities/budget-relations) as well as chunks, generate uses the configured prompt_template (v1 rag_response / naive_rag_response) instead of the two-line 'Context/Question' template, the priority_class config key is read or rem...

LightRAG retrieval matches v1 ordering and selection: entity-lookup searches with the low-level keyword string and relation-lookup with the high-level keyword string; expanded one-hop relations are sorted by (rank, weight) descending before budget truncation; chunk-sel-kg selects entity and relation chunks separately (relation chunks deduplicated against entity chunks) then round-robin merges t...

Query traces for the naive/hybrid/local/global LightRAG arms contain no no-op embedder-index node: the node is removed from query wirings (kept only in a recipe/index wiring) or is skipped and marked recipe-only, and it declares no calls_embedding/writes_artifact on a run where it did nothing.

The v1 driver ops 'entities' (entity map for a document_id) and 'entity_info' (entity details by name) are either reachable through an engine method plus REST route and MCP tool (e.g. a delete-impact preview listing entities a document contributes and which survive deletion), or deleted from the driver and test stub.

After a real HippoRAG ingest (chunk-embed writes), a query on the normal PPR path (fact-filter keeps at least one fact) returns items whose ids resolve: assemble-result hydrates non-empty content for every PPR-selected item, and Engine.resolve_evidence succeeds for every evidence ref in the envelope instead of raising UnresolvableEvidenceReferenceError. PPR item ids and chunk-embed vector/KV ke...

reset-vector-join's passage weights are keyed by the same strings as the graph's chunk vertex names, so ppr seeds each passage vertex whose chunk scored against the query with a non-zero reset weight (passage_node_weight times its score); the passage branch is no longer silently dropped (reset_vector_join.py:86-93, ppr.py:54-64).

When any node of an ingest wiring fails, Engine.ingest commits none of the staged writes: every store's drop_pending_index_ops runs instead of index_done_callback, so the HippoRAG chunk vectors, hipporag-text-chunks KV records and entity/fact vectors staged by earlier nodes (chunk-embed, entity-fact-embed) are absent afterwards; the 422 refusal is then raised (engine.py:731-761). graph-augment-...

A HippoRAG ingest refusal carries the real exception of the node that failed (e.g. ClientNotWiredError naming 'embedding' when chunk-embed has no embedding client), including the failing node id, instead of the synthesized RuntimeError "the 'ingest' node produced no result and no exception"; _node_result_or_refuse looks at every node exception recorded in the run, not only the provides node (en...

The fact-filter node receives the query text: fact-filter is listed in consumes_query of wirings/hipporag/base.json, and the LLM prompt it sends contains the query between ---Query--- and ---Candidate Facts---.

Every chunk produced by chunk-embed gets a passage vertex in the HippoRAG graph after ingest, including chunks for which OpenIE extracted no triples, so PPR can rank them (passage_edges.py:50-63, graph_augment_persist.py:61-77).

synonymy-edges matches the entities new in the current ingest against all entities, both those committed by earlier ingests and those staged by entity-fact-embed in the same run. After the first ingest of a document containing entities 'films' and 'movies' with cosine similarity above the threshold, the films-movies synonymy edge exists. A later ingest that adds no new entity similar to either ...

HippoRAG edge weights and edge_types accumulate across ingests: a co-occurrence edge produced by two separate ingests has the summed co-occurrence weight, and a later synonymy emission for the same pair adds its type and weight without discarding the stored co-occurrence count (graph_augment_persist.py:61-82, graph.py:291-296).

A fact extracted from different documents in separate ingests keeps the union of chunk_ids in both its fact vector metadata and its KV 'fact:<id>' record, so reset-vector-join's divisor and the fact's provenance reflect every source chunk (entity_fact_embed.py:139-163).

OpenIE extraction failures are reported: malformed NER or triple JSON responses and per-chunk chat() exceptions are counted per chunk and returned in the ingest outcome (and trace), so an ingest that extracted nothing is distinguishable from a successful one; NER/triple calls run with bounded concurrency instead of strictly serial (openie.py:72-108, 145-178).

A HippoRAG query returns at most top_k items and evidence refs (default stated in the wiring), with zero-score PPR vertices excluded; both the PPR branch and the DPR fallback apply the cut, so answer and evidence size do not grow with corpus size (dpr_fallback.py:65-69, ppr.py:84-89, assemble_result.py:58-65, engine.py:1053-1056).

A HippoRAG query run dispatches only query-side nodes (none of the seven index nodes from base.json:6-57 appear in the trace), the effect union used to select the query wiring contains no writes_vector/writes_kv/writes_graph/writes_artifact, and the query text is embedded exactly once per query (shared by fact-score, reset-vector-join and dpr-fallback).

The HippoRAG envelope answer is not an inline copy of evidence content (§18.2): the answer field has the same meaning as for LightRAG and the envelope no longer equals the retrieved chunk texts joined by blank lines (assemble_result.py:31-36, 52-65; engine.py:513).

Job, corpus and health status cover HippoRAG: GET /jobs/{job_id} for the job_id returned by a HippoRAG ingest returns a terminal status instead of 422 UnknownJobError; /corpus and /corpus/counts list and count HippoRAG documents when HippoRAG is selected; health probes the selected modality's stores (hipporag-chunks, hipporag-text-chunks, hipporag-graph) instead of only the LightRAG namespaces ...

HippoRAG supports document delete and clean re-ingest: delete_document with a HippoRAG selector removes the document's chunk vectors, KV records, passage vertices/edges and fact provenance instead of raising NoWritePathForModalityError; re-ingesting a document_id with shorter text leaves no chunk, vector, KV record or passage edge from ordinals beyond the new chunk count.

An EvidenceRef minted by a HippoRAG query never resolves silently to different text after the same document_id is re-ingested with changed content: it either resolves to the original text or fails with UnresolvableEvidenceReferenceError (chunk_embed.py:80, 96-114; evidence.py:6-20).

HippoRAG ingest token accounting never reports tokens from different counters under one counted_by label: summing accountings with mixed counted_by values yields one row per counter (or the unbudgetable sentinel), using one shared helper instead of the duplicated _sum_token_accountings in openie.py:118-131 and entity_fact_embed.py:59-70.

Every config key in wirings/hipporag/base.json and wirings/hipporag/corpus-ingest.json is either read by its part body or removed. The keys are entity-fact-embed namespaces, synonymy-edges guard, reset-vector-join socket_shape/arm_precedence/apportionment_policy, ppr readback and assemble-result order_policy. HippoRAG part docstrings and config text make no claim the code does not meet: reset-v...

When a HippoRAG query takes a declared degradation path (the fact-filter guard fires and the DPR fallback is used), the non-debug envelope reports it, without the consumer having to resolve the debug trace (assemble_result.py:22-30, engine.py:271-284, 1106-1109).

Each of the six query candidates (naive, bypass, hybrid, local, global, hipporag) can be resolved by at least one production §18.4 selector without a promote. Today capability matching with the stable fewest-nodes sort makes hybrid (17 nodes) and global (15 nodes, listed after local) unreachable, because both have local's effect union. The selectors.py module docstring (lines 10-25) states whic...

parse_wiring reports a named violation whenever a top-level provides entry or evidence_position.node names a node missing from the wiring's nodes. Every resolved wiring returned by all_wirings() passes that check. For bypass, which has no retrieval node, this means its evidence_position is removed or set to null instead of naming the removed chunk-vector. A local-arm /query that retrieves chunk...

ResponseEnvelope.stop_reason and degradation_reason, and the same two fields in the non-debug /trace/resolve output, never contain an internal node id, a part name@version, or an internal exception class name. A failed embedder-query or fact-score node produces a reason drawn from a fixed node-free vocabulary, and the node detail is shown only in the debug trace. The leak check matches substrings...

When no provides node produced a completion (a failed or partial run), ResponseEnvelope.depth_label is null instead of 'stage'. When a provides node answered, depth_label holds the depth chosen by the owner decision: either the wiring depth required by §18.2/R-1 or the answering node's depth.
